scope.description: Public leadership-verification safety under a network partition separating the old leader and a nonvoter from the two remaining voters in a three-voter configuration. A higher-term elected leader and completed new command precede invocation on the old leader. The proposition forbids success, but permits errors or remaining pending until bounded harness shutdown.
assumptions: Non-Byzantine actual Raft workers and transports; requests may be unavailable across a declared partition.
Static, consistently installed membership and stable participant IDs; no forced recovery, restore, or membership change during the comparison.
Observe real election and successful command application in the same execution; do not assign terms or role state.
The original leader has not rejoined or won another election before completion.
excluded: Proof of stale application reads, conflicting committed logs, crash durability, or every transport variant.
Treating absence of remote responses alone as proof of lost authority.

parameters.required_order: higher-term authority and applied command -> old-leader VerifyLeader invocation -> result

properties.reason: Independent applicability, correlated prerequisites and fully observed result comparison

adaptations: No target changes or critical state assignments. In-memory transport wrapper disables optional pipelining and records successful append responses by target ID.

Different valid per-node election/lease durations: old node and nonvoter use 3 seconds, other voters 150ms; all use 10ms commit timeout. These permit replacement election before the old lease expires; no lease worker is paused.
Network cuts use real InmemTransport.Disconnect, affecting every RPC crossing the partition. Already admitted requests may complete.
MockFSM records actual callback data; read-only locked inspection confirms the replacement command.
Read-only atomic latest-configuration and commit-index observations confirm installed membership/prefix; no private role or term writes.
boundaries: Proof of stale application reads, conflicting committed logs, crash durability, or every transport variant.
Treating absence of remote responses alone as proof of lost authority.
Only public VerifyLeader authority semantics are checked; stale application reads and conflicting logs are excluded.
The result is not correlated using an expected-to-change term: operation is the independent identity; term relationships are predecessor conditions.
Response counts are diagnostic only. Delayed pre-partition replies could affect the mechanism but cannot restore authority after the independently established newer election.
The transport has no heartbeat fast-path and optional pipelining is disabled; other transport modes are not covered.
A successful exploration with unchanged term and no replacement leader does not establish this antecedent.
The stronger legal prefix and public result require a new submitted check.
The measured comparison is bounded to the submitted partition and timing configuration; successful execution is not overall correctness.
